title: configure-custom-objects.html
content: Use the steps below to configure a custom object for SMS messaging. You will need to add a lookup field on the {{variable.Object_SMSMessage}} object and create a new field on the custom object. For this example, we are using the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} object. SMS Object Create a Custom Object Lookup Field Go to Setup. Click the Object Manager tab. In the Quick Find box, enter and click “SMS Message.” Click the Field & Relationships tab. Click {{variable.button_new}} . Select “Lookup Relationship” and click {{variable.Button_Next}} .   Set Related To to “Attendee” and click {{variable.Button_Next}} .   Enter the following information. {{variable.Field_Messaging_FieldLabel}} : “Attendee” {{variable.Field_Messaging_FieldName}} : “Attendee” Help Text : “The Attendee who is related to this SMS message” Child Relationship Name = “SMS_Message” Set the remaining fields based on your requirements.   Click {{variable.Button_Next}} . Select the profile access for this field. Click {{variable.Button_Next}} . Make sure the new field will be added to the page layout.   Click {{variable.Button_Next}} . Enter a Related List Label .   Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Messaging will now detect the relationship between the {{variable.Object_SMSMessage}} and {{variable.Object_Attendee}} objects. You can also add the Messaging Messenger component to this object's page and create SMS Templates for this object. Custom Object Create a Do Not SMS Field Go to Setup. Click the Object Manager tab. In the Quick Find box, enter and click “Attendee.” Click the Fields & Relationships tab. Click {{variable.button_new}} . Select “Checkbox” and click {{variable.Button_Next}} .   Enter the following information. {{variable.Field_Messaging_FieldLabel}} : “Do Not SMS” {{variable.Field_Messaging_FieldName}} : “Do_Not_SMS” Help Text : “Check this box to stop an SMS message from being sent to this Attendee.” Set the remaining fields based on your requirements.   Click {{variable.Button_Next}} . Select the profile access for this field. Click {{variable.Button_Next}} . Make sure the new field will be added to the page layout.   Click {{variable.Button_Save}} .   Create a Data Type Phone Field To send SMS messages to a custom object, the custom object needs a Phone field that has Data Type = "Phone." Messaging will not detect phone numbers in text fields. Go to Setup. Click the Object Manager tab. In the Quick Find box, enter and click “Attendee.” Click the Fields & Relationships tab. Click {{variable.button_new}} . Select “Phone” and click {{variable.Button_Next}} .   Enter the following information. {{variable.Field_Messaging_FieldLabel}} : “Phone” {{variable.Field_Messaging_FieldName}} : “SMS_Phone Help Text : "Use this phone number to send to send SMS messages.” Set the remaining fields based on your requirements.   Click {{variable.Button_Next}} . Select the profile access for this field. Click {{variable.Button_Next}} . Make sure the new field will be added to the page layout.   Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Lightning Update the Page Layout and Related List Add the Do Not SMS Field Go to Setup. Click the Object Manager tab. In the Quick Find box, search for and click “Attendee.” Click the Page Layouts tab. Select the layout type you need to update. Click the Fields tab. In the Quick Find box, search for the {{variable.Field_Lead_DoNotSMS}} field. Drag and drop the {{variable.Field_Lead_DoNotSMS}} field onto the page layout. Add the Related List Click the Related Lists tab. In the Quick Find box, search for the “SMS Messages” Related List. Drag and drop the Related List onto the page layout. Click the Wrench icon to open the Properties for this related list. Add these fields in the following order: {{variable.Field_SMS_RList_MessageDate}} {{variable.Field_SMS_RList_Direction}} {{variable.Field_SMS_RList_MessageFull}} {{variable.Field_SMS_RList_Status}} {{variable.Field_SMS_RList_FromPhone}} {{variable.Field_SMS_RList_ToPhone}} {{variable.Field_SMS_RList_SMSMsgNumber}} In the Sort By drop-down, choose "SMS Message Number" and "Descending". Click the plus sign (+) located in the Buttons section. Uncheck the box next to New and click Ok . Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Lightning Record Page Layout Click the Lightning Record Pages tab. Click the name of the layout you want to modify.  Click {{variable.Button_SF_Edit}} . If you don't see any Lightning page layouts listed, complete the following steps. Click {{variable.button_new}} .  Choose Record Page.  Click {{variable.Button_Next}} .  Enter a {{variable.Field_SF_PageLayout_Label}} (i.e. Attendee Layout).  Set {{variable.Field_SF_PageLayout_Object}} = “Attendee.”  Click {{variable.Button_Next}} .  Click the Clone Salesforce Default Page tab.  Choose a layout. Click Done . You should now be in the Lightning App Builder.  On the left-hand navigation bar, scroll down to the Custom-Managed section. Locate the Blackthorn Messaging Messenger component. Drag and drop the component onto the page layout.  The right-hand column will have the configuration options. We recommend keeping the {{variable.Field_SF_PageLayout_MaxHeight}} = "400px", but you can modify it as needed. If you've added the component to a sidebar, set {{variable.Field_SF_PageLayout_Columns}} = “One Column.” If you've added it to a wide section of the page, you can set {{variable.Field_SF_PageLayout_Columns}} = “Two Column” to maximize the space. Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Click Activation .  Review the settings. Click Close . Refresh your browser for the changes to take effect. Open an Attendee record to see the Blackthorn Messaging Messenger component on your page.
